# 5. Interaction Flow Based on the above functional architecture and the integration model of Agent/Copilot, this chapter focuses on how to achieve end-to-end processing of the IP Network single-domain fault management through the interaction and cooperation of agents at the Resource layer and the Service layer. ## 5.1. AN L4 IP Network Fault Management flow [Figure: Fig.2 AN L4 IP Network Fault Management Workflow] For faults that can be automatically repaired, the Agent operates in an autonomous closed-loop mode, without involving the FME Copilot.: - Step 1 represent the fault occurrence phase. - Step 2 represent the fault awareness, analysis, decision and execution phase. In the above example, the fault agent automatically performs fault identification, automatic diagnosis, and automatic repair. - Step 3a represent the archiving phase. In the above example, where the resource layer agent reports the fault incident and the handling results to the service layer’s fault management center, which then archives the information. For faults that require on-site repairs, the fault Agent automatically performs fault identification, conducts automated diagnostics, and generates repair recommendations. The FME uses Copilot to assist humans in carrying out on-site fault handling operations. - Step 1 represent the fault occurrence phase. - Step 2 represent the fault awareness, analysis, decision phase. In the above example, the fault agent automatically performs fault identification, automatic diagnosis, and automatic generate repair solution. - Step 3b to 6 represent the execution phase. In the above example, the resource layer agent sends the fault incident and the automatically generated handling recommendations to the service layer fault center. The fault center initiates a work order system to dispatch the work order to the FME. During the on-site handling process, the FME interacts with the service layer Copilot and resource layer Copilot via an app to obtain natural language-based repair guidance. ## 5.2.
